subject: Sequenced activation plan for AWS Private Offer — multi-buyer rollout & approval triggers
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@novamed.io>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novamed.io
Date: 2026-11-01 09:12 -0800
Subject: Private Offer activation window & buyer sequencing

Hi Grace / team,

Thanks again for walking NovaMed through the private offer terms yesterday. Procurement is ready to move but we need a concrete activation cadence and clarity on what triggers CFO signoff for multi-division rollouts. Two asks from our side:

1) A short runbook that shows a step-by-step activation for the first 3 buyer units (pilot -> staged -> full).
2) A clear list of approvals and the expected timing for CFO/legal to sign off so we can align our procurement calendar.

We want to stagger activation across three BU's over a 60-day window; please advise whether Redwood requires all buyers to be signed / DocuSigned before activation begins or if activation can be progressive with per-buyer activation.

Attached is our internal procurement policy snapshot (procurement@novamed.io). Happy to hop on a quick call this week if easier.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Director, IT Procurement
NovaMed

Attachment: NovaMed_Procurement_Policy.pdf (stated)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@novamed.io>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02 10:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Private Offer activation window & buyer sequencing

Hi Sarah — thanks for the note and the procurement snapshot.

Quick summary up front: progressive activation is supported. We recommend the following sequenced plan (high level):

- Day 0: Sign PO for pilot BU (DocuSign link to follow). Activate pilot SKU in region-us.
- Day 14: Validate onboarding signals (billing + token consumption + SLA checks).
- Day 21: Enable second BU with role-based access; issue consolidated invoice for pilot + BU2.
- Day 45: Confirm CFO approval signal for multi-division pricing; enable remaining BU(s).
- Day 60: Full tenant activation and runbook handoff to your Ops/Platform team.

Approvals required (minimal set):
- PO signature (procurement) — required to start pilot.
- Technical acceptance (your platform lead) — required to enable BU2.
- CFO signoff (for any pricing/term changes or expansion beyond pilot) — we can accept conditional activation pending CFO signoff for final pricing reconciliation.

I'm attaching an activation runbook draft and a short checklist that teams can use to gate each step. This is deliberately prescriptive to reduce back-and-forth during procurement.

If this plan looks good, we'll prepare a DocuSign packet that allows per-buyer acceptance and triggers (pilot -> staged -> full).

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Manager, Marketplace & GTM Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: PO_Activation_Runbook_v1.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03 14:40 -0800
Subject: Re: Private Offer activation window & buyer sequencing

Thanks Grace — this is helpful. A couple of operational questions from my side (finance/ops lens):

1) CFO signoff timing: if we permit progressive activation with conditional pricing reconciliation, we need a documented finance acceptance signal. Proposal: CFO can sign off on an "Activation Authorization" email once cumulative usage reaches X% of the committed pilot spend or at Day 30, whichever comes first. This prevents open-ended billing exposure.

2) Billing model: recommend we convert the pilot invoice to a consolidated monthly invoice and then pro-rate subsequent BU activations to the same billing period. That reduces complexity for NovaMed's AP team.

3) Escalation: include a 48-hour SLA for billing disputes during the staged period and a single point of contact ( finance-ops@redwood.com ) — we can add that to the runbook.

If the NovaMed procurement team is comfortable with this, I can draft the finance clause to insert into the DocuSign packet.

-Vivek
Head of Dedicated & Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@novamed.io>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04 11:20 -0800
Subject: Re: Private Offer activation window & buyer sequencing

Sarah — adding a short legal/compliance checklist from our side so procurement has what they need for evidence-based activation:

- Basic evidence: SOC 2 Type II summary (we've attached a one-page redacted summary).
- Data residency confirmation: NV region collection is supported for your tenant in us-west-2.
- Audit logs: we can provide 90 days of audit log exports on request.

Operational ask for NovaMed: please provide the following items before Day 14 validation so we can complete the staging gate:
- Technical contact for BU1 (name/email)
- Billing AP contact (name/email)
- CFO / Finance approver name & expected date window for the Activation Authorization email

I'll attach the SOC 2 summary in this thread. We should also confirm whether NovaMed needs any additional contractual terms (e.g., PO effective date vs activation date).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sr. Partnerships Manager, Marketplace Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOC2_evidence_summary.zip (attachment stub)

Grace/Ben/Vivek — this looks good and aligns with procurement's expectations. Quick responses:

- We will provide the BU1 technical contact by EOD Monday (Nov 8).
- CFO signoff: CFO prefers an Activation Authorization email; expected signoff window 11/25–11/30 (we will confirm exact date by next week).
- Billing: AP prefers consolidated monthly invoice with proration for BU additions — that matches Vivek's suggestion.

Next steps from Redwood: please send the DocuSign packet with the conditional activation language and attach the one-page SOC2 summary. Once we have the DocuSign ready, procurement will route to CFO for the Authorization window.

Appreciate the clear runbook — it makes coordination much easier.

Best,
Sarah Liu
